name: data_channel_envelope.v1
description: WebRTC data-channel message envelope (docs/13 §4): one native RTCDataChannel, label 'ctx', reliable and ordered, opened by the client inside the SDP offer. One channel, two streams split by type prefix: ctx.* carries context (client → server, plus the server's one recovery request), transcript.* and agent.state (server → client) drive the ConversationOverlay. Phase 3 sends only the server → client types; the ctx.* types are defined here now so the v1 envelope is complete — Phase 4 starts sending them (context capture). Forward compatibility (docs/13 §9): new message types are additive within v1, so a receiver MUST ignore messages whose type it does not recognize instead of erroring, and MUST ignore unknown envelope fields — which is why this schema deliberately does not set additionalProperties: false.

v.description: Envelope version. Breaking changes bump this to 2 in lockstep with the /v2 REST path and payload schema versions (docs/13 §9).

type.description: The v1 data-channel message set (docs/13 §4). Additive within v1: a client MUST ignore messages whose type is unknown (docs/13 §9).

seq.description: Per-direction monotonically increasing counter — the client → server ctx.* stream and the server → client stream each run their own (docs/13 §4). The backend gap-checks the client's single counter across the ctx.* stream (a lost delta corrupts merge state); the client never gap-checks the server stream (a lost caption partial is repaired by the next partial; a lost agent.state by the next transition).

payload.description: Per-type payload — see $defs, dispatched by the oneOf below.

ctx_snapshot_payload.description: client → server (Phase 4). Full screen_context/v1 IR, replacing server state wholesale; 300 ms debounce, forced on screen change and gap recovery (docs/13 §4). The IR's shape authority is docs/07 and protocol/schemas/screen_context.v1.json when it lands — this envelope schema deliberately does not re-define it, and only pins the payload version marker.

ctx_delta_payload.description: client → server (Phase 4). Changed components only, base_seq-verified merge; 300 ms debounce (docs/13 §4). Component shape authority is docs/07 / screen_context.v1.json.

base_seq.description: seq of the last snapshot or delta this delta applies on top of — NOT simply the previous message's seq, because ctx.event shares the single counter without advancing screen state (docs/13 §4).

last_action.description: The user action that produced this delta, when there was one (docs/07 last_action shape).

ctx_event_payload.description: client → server (Phase 4). One app_event/v1 timeline entry, sent immediately with no debounce (docs/13 §4). Event shape authority is docs/07/08 and protocol/schemas/app_event.v1.json when it lands; only the fields every event variant carries are pinned here.

ts.description: When the event happened on-device, epoch milliseconds — distinct from the envelope ts (when the message was sent).

ctx_request_snapshot_payload.description: server → client (Phase 4). Sent on a sequence gap in the client's ctx.* stream: asks for a fresh capture, not a replay (docs/13 §4).

last_good_seq.description: Last client seq the server ingested cleanly.

transcript_payload.description: server → client, shared by transcript.partial and transcript.final. The overlay keys captions on (turn, role): each transcript.partial replaces the previous partial for that key; transcript.final (once per (turn, role)) freezes it as the authoritative caption text (docs/13 §4). User-side partials are STT interims throttled to ~5/s; agent-side partials arrive per sentence, as dispatched to TTS.

agent_state_payload.description: server → client, on transition. Drives the overlay's listening/thinking/speaking indicator; the overlay renders state, never infers it (docs/13 §4).
